definitions.definition: The product of an object's mass and its velocity.
distractors: The product of an object's mass and its acceleration.
The rate of change of velocity.
The product of the net force acting on an object and the time for which it acts.
The energy an object possesses due to its motion.
The resistance of an object to a change in its state of motion.
The force required to keep an object moving at a constant velocity.

definitions.term: Newton's Second Law of Motion in terms of Momentum
definitions.definition: The net (or resultant) force acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of momentum of the object in the direction of the net force.
distractors: When object A exerts a force on object B, object B simultaneously exerts an oppositely directed force of equal magnitude on object A.
A body will remain in its state of rest or motion at constant velocity unless a non-zero net force acts on it.
The total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant in magnitude and direction.
The net work done on an object is equal to the change in the object's kinetic energy.
The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to its mass and inversely proportional to the net force.
The product of the net force and the time interval is equal to the change in momentum.

definitions.definition: The product of the resultant/net force acting on an object and the time the net force acts on the object.
distractors: The rate of change of momentum of an object.
The product of an object's mass and its velocity.
The force exerted on an object over a specific distance.
The total kinetic energy of an object before a collision.
The internal force that prevents an object from deforming during a collision.
The work done to stop an object over a certain time period.

definitions.definition: Impulse is equal to the change in momentum of the object.
distractors: Impulse is equal to the rate of change of momentum.
The total impulse in an isolated system is zero.
Impulse is inversely proportional to the time of contact.
Impulse is equal to the final momentum minus the initial kinetic energy.
The change in momentum is equal to the total mechanical energy of the system.
The product of force and distance equals the change in momentum.

definitions.term: Principle of Conservation of Linear Momentum
definitions.definition: The total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant (is conserved) in magnitude and direction.
distractors: The total kinetic energy of an isolated system remains constant.
The total mechanical energy of an isolated system remains constant.
The momentum of an individual object in a system remains constant during a collision.
The total momentum of a system is always zero before and after a collision.
The net force acting on an isolated system is equal to the total momentum.
The rate of change of momentum of an isolated system is constant.

definitions.definition: A system on which the net external force is zero.
distractors: A system in which no energy is transferred to the surroundings.
A system where only conservative forces do work.
A system containing only one object.
A system in which all objects are at rest.
A system where both momentum and kinetic energy are always conserved.
A system that is completely isolated from all internal forces.

definitions.definition: A collision in which both total momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved.
distractors: A collision in which only total momentum is conserved.
A collision in which the objects stick together after colliding.
A collision in which kinetic energy is converted into sound and heat.
A collision where the final velocity is zero.
A collision where the total kinetic energy increases.
A collision between two objects of equal mass.

definitions.definition: A collision during which kinetic energy is not conserved.
distractors: A collision during which momentum is not conserved.
A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
A collision where the objects bounce off each other with equal velocities.
A collision that only occurs in a non-isolated system.
A collision where the net force is zero.
A collision where total mechanical energy is conserved.

proportionality.statement: According to the impulse-momentum theorem, to achieve a specific change in momentum, if the time of impact is increased...
proportionality.correct: the average net force required is decreased.
distractors: the average net force required is increased.
the change in velocity must increase.
the mass of the object must decrease.
the total kinetic energy must remain constant.
the impulse will decrease proportionally.
the final velocity will decrease.

proportionality.statement: If the velocity of an object is doubled while its mass remains constant, its momentum will...
distractors: halve.
quadruple.
remain the same.
increase by a factor of four.
decrease exponentially.
become zero.

proportionality.statement: If both the mass and the velocity of an object are doubled, its momentum will...
distractors: double.
halve.
remain the same.
become eight times greater.
increase by a factor of $1/4$.
increase exponentially.

concepts.question: Which of the following statements best explains the purpose of crumple zones in modern cars?
concepts.correct: They increase the time of the collision, thereby decreasing the net force exerted on the passengers for a given change in momentum.
distractors: They decrease the time of the collision, thereby decreasing the net force exerted on the passengers.
They decrease the change in momentum of the car during the collision.
They ensure that the collision is completely elastic.
They absorb the total momentum of the car so the passengers experience zero impulse.
They decrease the mass of the car during impact.
They increase the net force to bring the car to a stop faster.

concepts.question: During a collision in an isolated system, which of the following quantities is always conserved?
distractors: Total kinetic energy.
The velocity of each individual object.
The momentum of each individual object.
Total mechanical energy.
The net force acting on the system.
The acceleration of the center of mass.

concepts.question: Two objects of different masses collide head-on in an isolated system. How do the impulses they experience compare?
concepts.correct: They experience impulses of equal magnitude but opposite direction.
distractors: The object with the larger mass experiences a larger impulse.
The object with the smaller mass experiences a larger impulse.
They experience impulses of equal magnitude and the same direction.
The impulse depends on their initial velocities.
The object with the higher initial kinetic energy experiences the larger impulse.
Neither object experiences an impulse because the system is isolated.
